sampling_model.design: Known clean design \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), observed only through a full-record Huber mixture.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) observed records are independent draws from \(R=(1-\epsilon)P+\epsilon Q\).
sampling_model.overlap: The propensity vanishes only on the boundary \(x_1=0\) and has polynomial order \(\kappa\) with calibration in \([1/4,1/2]\).
sampling_model.outcome: The clean outcome is bounded in \([0,1]\); only its two conditional means are Hölder-restricted.
sampling_model.contamination: The law \(Q\) may jointly corrupt \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\), including by placing atoms on the clean null boundary.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L,\epsilon\) and the clean covariate design, but not \(P,Q,u,\mu_0,\mu_1\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Unbounded inverse weights can make a point-identified treatment-effect parameter irregular, with rates governed by relative tail behavior.
Huber minimax lower bounds are governed by the clean risk and a total-variation modulus, while Scheffé tournaments attain optimal full-law total-variation rates.
Projection-based higher-order influence-function estimators attain optimal clean rates for missing-response means under low nuisance regularity.
An empirically estimated Gram operator yields a semiparametrically efficient clean higher-order estimator without smoothness of the covariate density.
Density-power IPW and doubly robust equations resist outcome outliers under stronger overlap and require an additional correction to retain double robustness.
A second-order correction can match an ATE nuisance-product frontier in a clean hybrid smoothness and structure-agnostic model.
Bias-corrected trimming supports ATE estimation and inference under limited overlap and is implemented for right-heart-catheterization data.
Low-rank structure permits data cleaning and causal inference under structured measurement error, missingness, discretization, and privacy noise with bounded propensities.
Section 3 constructs a trimmed bias-corrected doubly robust estimator from i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies the ATE-specific boundary conditions under clean sampling.

body.tldr: On the exact one-dimensional Lipschitz boundary class with \(e(x)=x^2u(x)\), a total finite dyadic cell estimator attains the same-experiment minimax risk \(n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\) when an arbitrary Huber contaminant may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). The theorem includes an explicit pre-optimization bound, global contaminant-mass accounting for point and diffuse corruption, and clean and neighborhood-colliding lower pairs. The causal bridge and total-variation modulus support this field-tier calibration, while the multidimensional smoothness phase diagram remains a first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: Section 3 and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 analyze trimming and boundary bias correction under clean i.i.d. sampling, while robust causal estimators treat narrower outcome corruption under stronger overlap and generic Huber theory does not preserve fast scalar-functional structure. No located theorem gives a computable same-class minimax equality when the propensity vanishes quadratically and \(Q\) may replace \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\).
project_justification.niche: The missing field-tier benchmark is a boundary reconstruction that remains stable when contaminating mass is concentrated exactly in its lowest-occupancy slab, with a converse built inside the same full-record mixture experiment.
project_justification.fill: The dyadic estimator uses variable-width cells, bounded zero-count-safe arm means, and a reused first slab to attain \(n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\). Exact clean-law pairs certify the clean and contamination lower bounds, and the remaining multidimensional projection frontier is stated separately as open content.

body.related_work: MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 is the nearest clean-record comparator. Section 3 defines its trimming and bias-corrected estimator from i.i.d. observations, and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies the ATE-specific boundary conditions; neither part allows arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). KhanTamer2010 establishes generic support-tail irregularity for inverse weighting but does not supply the controlled factorization \(e(x)=x_1^\kappa u(x)\), its calibration envelope, or a contaminated minimax theorem. ChenGaoRen2016 supplies robust tests and the Huber-neighborhood total-variation-modulus template, while its constructive upper theorem estimates whole laws rather than this scalar ATE at its clean functional rate. RobinsEtAl2017HOEE and LiuMukherjeeNeweyRobins2017EmpiricalHOIF supply projection and empirical Gram constructions under clean sampling; they inform only the open multidimensional route. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024 clarifies clean second-order ATE correction under interior overlap. HaradaFujisawa2024 controls outcome outliers but excludes arbitrary covariate and treatment-label replacement. MaEtAl2024Missing studies finite-coordinate missingness rather than continuous selection at a propensity zero. AgarwalSingh2022 uses structured low-rank corruption and bounded propensity. SasakiUra2022ET and SasakiUra2022Robustate motivate trimming and boundary correction under clean records, with the latter supplying the right-heart-catheterization consumer. HorowitzManski1995 explains why fixed contamination leaves irreducible ambiguity in the clean target.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Boundary-contamination diagnostic: for \(B=[h,2h]\), \(u=1/4\), clean treated-arm mean \(1/2\), and \(Q=\delta_{(h,1,1)}\), the clean treated mass in \(B\) is \(7h^3/12\). The resulting population shift of the boundary contribution is exactly \(h\epsilon/[2\{(1-\epsilon)7h^3/12+\epsilon\}]\), which is of order \(h^2=\epsilon^{1/2}\) at \(h=\epsilon^{1/4}\); the same global \(Q\)-mass accounting in the theorem covers diffuse contamination within a cell.
body.honest_scope: The field-tier headline is exactly the one-dimensional calibration \(\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;1,1,1,2,L)\asymp_L n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\), with a total finite estimator and matching same-experiment converse authored as results to prove. The causal bridge is standard support, and the Bernoulli reduction and total-variation modulus are supporting results. The general \(d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa\) rate formula, equality-boundary logarithms, robust projected correction, and matching full-class converse remain open. For \(\epsilon=0\), the calibration reduces to the clean \(n^{-2/5}\) frontier; for fixed nonzero \(\epsilon\), no statement claims point identification of \(\theta(P)\) from \(R\).
